Class RandomStrings

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.core.random.RandomStrings
public final class RandomStrings extends Object
Random strings: identifiers, tokens and codes made of characters taken at random in an alphabet. 
var secure = new SecureRandom();
RandomStrings.token(128, secure);                               // "pP3X2nq0GkTzvB-fL8_hJw", 128 bits
RandomStrings.string(8, RandomStrings.UNAMBIGUOUS, secure);     // "K7WQ4MZX", a code to read aloud
RandomStrings.string(6, RandomStrings.DIGITS, secure);          // "042917"

A string that must not be guessed, such as a session identifier or a password reset token, needs a source of randomness that cannot be predicted: a SecureRandom, not a seeded generator.

Each character calls RandomGenerator.nextInt(int) once with the size of the alphabet, and is the character at that index, so that every character of the alphabet has the same chance.

Since:
0.2.0

  • Method Details

    • token

      public static String token(int bits, RandomGenerator random)
      Returns a random string made of the characters of URL_SAFE, long enough to be one among at least 2^bits equally likely ones.
      Parameters:
      bits - the least number of bits of randomness: 128 or more for a string that must not be guessed
      random - the source of randomness
      Returns:
      a string of length(bits, URL_SAFE) characters
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if bits is negative

    • string

      public static String string(int length, String alphabet, RandomGenerator random)
      Returns a random string of a given length, made of characters of an alphabet.
      Parameters:
      length - the number of characters
      alphabet - the characters to take from
      random - the source of randomness
      Returns:
      the string
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if length is negative, or if alphabet is empty, has a character twice, which would be taken twice as often, or has a surrogate

    • length

      public static int length(int bits, String alphabet)
      Returns how many characters of an alphabet a random string needs, to be one among at least 2^bits equally likely ones.
      Parameters:
      bits - the least number of bits of randomness
      alphabet - the characters to take from
      Returns:
      the least length
      Throws:
